correctness.rationale: The group-inverse equations produce an idempotent projector whose image and kernel equal those of the matrix, forcing a free image/kernel splitting over a commutative local ring. Conversely an automorphism on one free summand and zero on its complement has the explicit group inverse obtained by inverting the automorphism. Orbit-stabilizer counts ordered decompositions, cancellation of the image automorphism factor yields |GL_n(R)|/|GL_{n-r}(R)|, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal contributes exactly |m|^{n^2-(n-r)^2}. The fixed-residue fiber count follows from |m|^{2r(n-r)} decomposition lifts and |m|^{r^2} automorphism lifts. The packaged checker verifies the defining equations exhaustively for all 2-by-2 matrices over Z/4Z and F_2[epsilon]/(epsilon^2).

originality.rationale: The inspected generalized-inverse sources give qualitative existence/formula results, while the closest finite-local enumeration source treats idempotents. None of the checked statements gives the rank-stratified group-invertible census or the nullity-squared lift survival law for arbitrary finite commutative local rings.
residual_risks: An older finite-semigroup enumeration may use “index-one regular elements” or a similar term rather than “group-invertible matrices” and therefore evade the terminology-based searches.

The local-ring theorem is structurally elementary once the image/kernel characterization of a group inverse is recognized; originality is claimed for the exact finite-local rank spectrum and uniform lifting law, not for the underlying group-inverse decomposition itself.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete natural invariant—the Drazin-index-one rank spectrum—for every full matrix ring over a finite commutative local ring. The fixed-residue lift law |m|^{-k^2} isolates exactly how singularity obstructs group invertibility under nilpotent thickening and shows that nonisomorphic rings with the same residue and radical sizes have identical spectra. This is a structural universality statement, not a single small-ring computation; the Z/4Z and dual-number census merely stress-tests it.
